endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Use the Patient and Family Advisory Councils Blueprint to help guide your organization through the process of forming and maintaining a successful PFAC.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence needs better health systems to reduce inequalities
endorsements.quote: In practice, this requires institutional channels, including citizen assemblies, standing patient and public involvement panels, and statutory consultation obligations on regulators, that give affected communities a formal role in shaping which AI tools are approved, how they are deployed, and under what conditions they are withdrawn.

endorsements.title: Six Interventions for the Responsible and Ethical Implementation of Medical AI Agents
endorsements.quote: We invite healthcare professionals and patient advocates to contribute real-world dilemmas for benchmarking and urge funders to support these efforts.

endorsements.title: Recommendations for Successful Development and Implementation of Digital Health Technology Tools
endorsements.quote: An advisory board can provide continuous feedback and support.

endorsements.title: Patient Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging
endorsements.quote: Patient advisory boards: establish advisory boards composed of diverse patient representatives to ensure patient concerns and priorities are integrated into decisions about AI development and implementation, including input on algorithm design, ethical guidelines, and clinical workflows.

endorsements.title: Reframing Justice in Healthcare AI: An Ubuntu-Based Approach for Africa
endorsements.quote: We propose engaging community advisory boards following the “Made in Africa AI” approach that prioritizes community‐driven, participatory methods and indigenous definitions of success [ 83 ].

endorsements.title: Health Equity Considerations in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
endorsements.quote: For example, if a hospital uses AI to help draft patient messages and responses, input should be solicited from community or patient advisory boards that reflect the demographics of the population served.

endorsements.title: Advancing Global Nursing Policy: AI-Driven Health Literacy Innovations for Migrant Domestic Workers
endorsements.quote: Practical approaches include community‐based participatory research workshops held on MDWs’ rest days at accessible venues (Israel et al. 2010 ), focus groups organized by language and country of origin to capture diverse perspectives, iterative prototype testing with real users to refine usability, and standing advisory panels that keep MDW voices central even after initial development ends.

endorsements.title: Partnerships to advance patient safety and address preventable harm: case studies from international health care leaders
endorsements.quote: At the organizational level, health systems across the world have introduced opportunities for patients, families, and caregivers to give feedback on their care engagement plans and other operational considerations that can identify potential or actual harm.

endorsements.title: Moving beyond the benchmarks: Five foundational principles for meaningful AI evaluation in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Establish a patient advisory board including diverse socioeconomic backgrounds, not just educated/insured

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied here tests whether a patient and family advisory council improves an organization's decisions about AI or the outcomes of AI use, and no study documents harm from the absence of such a forum. The recommendation rests on one governance framework and seven commentaries.

perspectives.view: Eight sources endorse the practice, and all use "should" language. One is a framework (CHAI) and seven are commentaries. No included study tests an advisory council for AI oversight, and none measures the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, expert opinion without empirical tests cannot support a certainty rating, so this recommendation has no direct evidence.

Four commentaries ask that councils reflect the population served or include people from lower socioeconomic backgrounds and people without insurance. One describes sessions organized by language and held at accessible times for migrant workers. No supplied study tests these proposals or shows whether such councils recruit or retain underserved members or whether their input changes AI decisions.

commentary.research_gap: Studies could compare organizations with and without AI-focused patient councils on measurable outcomes, such as changes to AI tool selection or configuration, patient-reported trust, complaint rates, and detection of AI-related safety events. They could also record council composition, meeting burden, and cost. Descriptive work documenting how often the absence of a patient forum leads to missed problems would establish whether the hazard occurs in practice.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Several endorsing commentaries call for including these groups, but whether councils reach them or represent their concerns in AI decisions remains untested.
